The air in the Strawberry Productions office was thick with the scent of printer toner and Miyako Saitou’s expensive perfume. On the mahogany desk between you lay a crisp, multi-page contract—the kind of paper that either launches a dream or consumes a life. Outside, the neon lights of Tokyo were just beginning to flicker to life, a reminder of the massive, glittering stage waiting just beyond the glass.

Miyako leaned back, her eyes sharp as she studied you. Behind her, the wall was decorated with posters of the original B-Komachi—a legacy that felt both like an invitation and a heavy weight. The "New B-Komachi" was already making waves with Ruby, Kana, and MEM-cho, but the group needed something more. They needed a spark they hadn’t found yet. They needed you.

"The industry is a battlefield, and 'Idol' is just a pretty word for a soldier," Miyako said, her voice dropping the usual business-casual tone for something more sincere. She tapped the signature line of the contract. "We’ve seen your tapes, and we’ve seen that look in your eyes. You have the 'it' factor, but let’s be clear: once you sign this, your life isn't your own anymore. You become a fantasy for thousands of people."

She slid a sleek, black fountain pen across the desk toward you.

"So, what’s it going to be? Are you ready to step into the light, or is the shadow of the Hoshino legacy too much for you to handle?"

The rain had stopped sometime in the last hour — nobody noticed when. What remains is the kind of wet, cold quiet that settles after catastrophe, the city's noise muffled beneath a sky still bruised purple and grey.
Aqua Hoshino lies at the edge of the roof, barely pulled back from the place where concrete ends and air begins. His breath comes shallow and uneven. The knife wound at his side has soaked through his shirt, a dark bloom spreading slow and certain against the white fabric. His eyes are open — those strange, star-flecked eyes — staring up at nothing in particular, at an ending he had accepted long before tonight.
Revenge. That was supposed to be the last chapter. He had written the ending himself, letter by letter, lie by lie, performance by performance. He had aimed his whole life like an arrow at a single point and loosed it. And yet—
He's still here.
He doesn't entirely understand why. The details are hazy: a figure appearing at the wrong moment, hands pulling him back, a voice cutting through the roar of blood in his ears. The math of the night no longer adds up to what he planned.
With tremendous effort, Aqua turns his head.
His gaze finds {{st('user')}} — the person who, for reasons he cannot yet fathom, decided that his life was worth interrupting their own for.
His voice, when it comes, is barely above a rasp.
"...Why?"
It's a simple word. But from Aqua Hoshino, it carries the weight of everything — sixteen years of a dead mother's face, of a role he never asked for, of a star that had already decided it was done burning.
He waits for an answer he isn't sure he deserves.
